sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Koeberlinia spinosa is an evergreen shrub of arid regions in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It is usually 2.4–4.6 m tall and may approach 7 m. Its green branches carry out much of its photosynthesis.

sections.title: Branches, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The leaves are small and soon fall; the branch tips bear sharp spines. The pale flowers are tiny. The fruits are black berries about 6 mm across, eaten by birds.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Birds eating the fruits does not establish that they are safe for people. The sources consulted do not document a reliable human food use; do not eat them.
